external_sources.title: Childline: Asking an adult for help
external_sources.supports: Choose a trusted adult, plan a message, use speech or a note, and seek another adult if needed. Adults may need to share a safety concern with people who can help.

external_sources.title: PSHE Association: Handling complex issues safely
external_sources.supports: Use ground rules, distanced examples, a right to pass and appropriate safeguarding responses.

external_sources.title: NHS: Poisoning
external_sources.supports: Possible poisoning, unconsciousness or severe breathing problems need emergency help. Do not make a person vomit or give food or drink after suspected poisoning. Follow emergency-service instructions.

vocab.definition: The chance that harm could happen.
Something we know or can check.

cases.text: Alex misses the bus. The club reception is still staffed.
cases.fact: There is a staffed place to ask for help.
cases.next_step: Go to reception and ask staff to help contact a trusted adult.
cases.staff_note: Do not prescribe a route to a real pupil or collect their journey details.

cases.text: An unknown online contact offers a lift and asks for Alex’s location.
cases.fact: The person and lift are not verified.
cases.next_step: Do not accept or share location; ask a trusted adult to help.
cases.staff_note: Friendliness, profile pictures and follower counts do not prove identity.

cases.text: A friend suggests a shortcut through a closed building site.
cases.fact: The site is closed and access is not permitted.
cases.next_step: Stay out and use an agreed open route.
cases.staff_note: Do not explore a real site or ask pupils to act out trespass.

cases.text: A collection plan changes. Sam is unsure who will arrive.
cases.fact: The new collector has not been confirmed.
cases.next_step: Stay with staff and check the change through the agreed contact route.
cases.staff_note: Use school collection procedures. Do not make up a promise that a particular adult will attend.

cases.text: Someone pressures Jo to go somewhere after Jo has said no.
cases.fact: Jo’s boundary is not being respected.
cases.next_step: Move towards a suitable safe, staffed place and seek adult help.
cases.staff_note: Do not imply that refusal alone prevents harm. Responsibility belongs to the person causing harm.

cases.text: A person nearby collapses and cannot be woken.
cases.next_step: Call 999 and get adult help now.
cases.staff_note: Follow emergency-service instructions; do not practise physical first aid or make a real call in class.

PSHE-LAUNCH-A2-W03 · Monday 16–Friday 20 November 2026
Staff brief: 0 minutes.

Model and hinge

Alex misses the bus after a club. Fact: the planned ride has gone. Risk: being stuck without safe travel. Alex goes to the club’s staffed reception. Alex asks staff to help contact a trusted adult. They check a safe travel plan together.

B. The driver and offer are not verified. Alex should remain in a suitable staffed place and ask a trusted adult to help check an agreed travel option. A friendly tone is not evidence of safety. Reteach with an unexpected change to a collection plan. Do not teach that all strangers are dangerous or that familiar people cannot cause harm.
Individual evidence key

Credit an explicit clue, a plausible risk and an action that reduces it, plus an adult/support route. For A use staffed reception; B do not accept an unverified lift; C avoid the closed site; D confirm through staff; E seek support for ignored boundaries; F call 999. Do not award certainty from an unsupported guess or blame a victim.
Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: Do not prescribe a route to a real pupil or collect their journey details.
Card B: Friendliness, profile pictures and follower counts do not prove identity.
Card C: Do not explore a real site or ask pupils to act out trespass.
Card D: Use school collection procedures. Do not make up a promise that a particular adult will attend.
Card E: Do not imply that refusal alone prevents harm. Responsibility belongs to the person causing harm.
Card F: Follow emergency-service instructions; do not practise physical first aid or make a real call in class.
Common misunderstandings

A hazard is a potential cause of harm; risk is the chance of harm. Familiarity and friendliness do not guarantee safety. A safer plan reduces risk but cannot guarantee nothing will happen. Someone who is harmed is not to blame for another person’s behaviour.
Teaching boundary

Use fictional situations and a pass option. Do not rehearse threats, harassment, being followed or a collapse. Avoid victim-blaming. Listen calmly to a real concern and follow local safeguarding arrangements separately from learning evidence. Emergency examples are verbal only.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
